summary.text: A 70-year-old man presented with one month of progressive dyspnea and weakness, low-grade pyrexia of 37.8°C, and an unremarkable physical examination. Blood tests showed normocytic anemia, elevated CRP, D-dimer 9840 ug/L and CA125 312.1 U/ml, and imaging revealed extensive pulmonary lesions, a large right atrial mass invading the superior vena cava, pleural effusion and left subclavian lymphadenopathy.

Thoracentesis showed bloody exudative fluid without malignant cells, and lung and lymph node pathology were nondiagnostic. PET/CT showed focal uptake in the right atrial mass with SUVmax 5.8 and scattered lung and pleural uptake. An ICE-guided right atrial biopsy of five samples yielded two diagnostic for EHE, and histopathology with CD34, CD31 and ERG expression confirmed cardiac epithelioid hemangioendothelioma.

A multidisciplinary team recommended chemotherapy and targeted therapy without mass resection. The patient deteriorated quickly because of aggressive pulmonary lesions and had severe dyspnea, with recurrent bloody pleural effusion shown on imaging one month after hospitalization, and decided to receive hospice care.

summary.text: A 50-year-old woman had four months of shortness of breath and chest tightness and was admitted to a nearby hospital, where chest CT showed an enlarged heart, pericardial effusion and multiple lung lesions with suspected infection. CT-guided needle biopsy of the pulmonary lesions was unremarkable; after a few days she gradually felt dyspnea and weakness, and she was transferred to our cardiology department for a conclusive diagnosis.

Blood tests showed a high CRP of 16.6 mg/L, pro-BNP 224 pg/mL, D-dimer 2050 ug/L and CA125 60.1 U/ml. Imaging showed multiple lung lesions and a large irregular right atrial mass invading the superior vena cava. A cardiac malignant tumor with extensive lung metastases was suspected, and ICE-guided right atrial biopsy histopathology confirmed cardiac angiosarcoma with CD34, CD31, Fli-1 and ERG positivity and Ki-67 60%.

After transfer to the oncology unit she was advised chemotherapy and targeted therapy without mass removal and was treated with paclitaxel, liposomal doxorubicin and anlotinib. After 5 courses of chemotherapy, the lateral wall of the right atrium was no longer occupied and the number of lung metastases was reduced.

summary.text: A 62-year-old man was transferred to cardiology with chest tightness and recurrent pericardial effusion for two months. Chest CT at a local emergency room showed an enlarged cardiac shadow, massive pericardial effusion and interstitial pulmonary edema; bloody pericardial effusion was drained by pericardiocentesis and diuretics and antihypertensives were given. After one month the effusion increased significantly again with obvious chest tightness.

After admission to our hospital a second pericardiocentesis yielded 900 ml of bloody fluid in total. Blood tests shortly after admission showed high levels of CRP, pro-BNP, D-dimer and CA125. Echocardiography, enhanced CMR and chest CT showed a mass at the junction of the right atrium and ventricle, and pathological analysis of the pericardial effusion found no tumor cells.

ICE-guided atrial biopsy was done without complications and histology with CD34, CD31, Fli-1 and ERG expression confirmed cardiac epithelioid hemangioendothelioma. With rapid progression of the pericardial effusion and significant dyspnea, the patient eventually discontinued getting treatment.

(B) Chest enhanced CT, and (C) Cardiac enhanced-MRI revealed a large mass (arrow) at the junction of the RA and RV. (D) Catheter for intracardiac echocardiography (arrowhead) and cardiac bioptome (arrow). (E) The intracardial echocardiography demonstrates well-targeted biopsy catheter (arrow) on the mass. (F) Histopathological imaging revealed small vascular lumen formed by single cell, and cardiac epithelioid hemangioendothelioma (EHE) was diagnosed.
